title: Exact pullback: resolving-model identification with exact localization
statement:
Let $(\mathcal C,R)$ and $(\mathcal D,S)$ be ringed sites small relative to a common universe of ordinary module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Let $u^{-1}\dashv u_*$ be a geometric morphism, with $u^{-1}$ preserving finite limits and a homomorphism of commutative ring sheaves $u^{-1}R\to S$. Put $F(M)=S\otimes_{u^{-1}R}u^{-1}M$ [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], and assume $F$ exact. Use unbounded derived categories with localization functors $q_R,q_S$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. A resolving complex means a K-flat complex with flat terms [def-pc-kflat-complex, def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules].

Let $L=Lu^*$ and $\epsilon_A:L(q_RA)\to q_S(FA)$ be the canonical derived pullback and its natural comparison, with $e_P=\epsilon_P$ invertible on resolving complexes [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pullback]. Let $U=D(F)$ and $\kappa_A:U(q_RA)\cong q_S(FA)$ be the exact localization and its factorization [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization]. Give $L$ the shift comparisons obtained by shifting resolving complexes and $U$ those induced by the identity termwise maps $F(A[n])\cong(FA)[n]$, for every $n\in\mathbf Z$.

Then $F$ preserves flat module sheaves and resolving complexes, and preserves every small direct sum, including the infinite diagonal sums in unbounded total tensors. For every module morphism $v$ and integer $z$, $F(zv)=zF(v)$; the termwise functor preserves the differential signs $(-1)^n$, all integer shift signs and Koszul interchange signs.

Every $\epsilon_A$ is invertible. There is a unique natural isomorphism $\eta:L\xrightarrow{\sim}U$ satisfying $\kappa_P\eta_{q_RP}=e_P$ for every resolving $P$. In fact $\kappa_A\eta_{q_RA}=\epsilon_A$ for every complex $A$, without any flatness or boundedness hypothesis on $A$. This isomorphism commutes with all integer shift comparisons. For every module sheaf $M$, it identifies the degree-zero comparison $L(M[0])\cong(FM)[0]$ given by $\epsilon_{M[0]}$ with the exact-localization comparison $U(M[0])\cong(FM)[0]$, including when $M$ is not flat.

proof.text: The specified ringed-topos pullback preserves coefficient-sized filtered colimits. For an index set iota, express its coproduct as the filtered colimit, over finite subsets, of finite subcoproducts. F preserves the latter by finite-colimit preservation. Build the cocone on the images of finite subcoproducts by their universal properties. Its universal map satisfies the coproduct equations by restriction to singleton subsets; uniqueness follows by testing all finite summand inclusions. This proves preservation of coproducts without a universe-restricted module-adjunction presentation.

source.place: Tag 015F, exact-functor setting; filtered-to-coproduct assembly by the agent from Mathlib Limits.Constructions.Filtered.

proof.text: Apply Mathlib additive-functor map_zsmul to F and to its termwise complex functor. These are precisely the integer-sign equations in the Lean statement.

Choose a flat-term K-flat resolution p:P→A. The source localization sends p to an isomorphism, and so does F followed by target localization, by exact factorization. The comparison epsilon is invertible at P by he. Its naturality square makes the composite of L(q(p)) with epsilon_A invertible; cancel L(q(p)) to conclude that epsilon_A is invertible.

The exact factorization kappa exhibits mapDerivedCategory as a left derived functor: an invertible localization factorization is its right Kan extension. Apply Mathlib leftDerivedUnique with hL to construct eta. The leftDerivedNatTrans factorization identity is the all-complex normalization equation. To prove uniqueness from resolving normalization, compare the two hom natural transformations. For every A, choose p:P→A as above; cancel G(q(p)) in their naturality squares to reduce equality at A to equality at P. Localization faithfulness extends this equality to every derived object. Cancel kappa_P to obtain equality on resolving representatives, then use this determination argument.

source.place: Tags 06YS and 015F; Mathlib leftDerivedUnique and localization faithfulness.

proof.text: For each integer n, the desired shift square is an equality of natural transformations from shift[n] followed by L to exact localization followed by shift[n]. By the resolving determination argument in the preceding step it suffices to test resolving P. Substitute the global factorization epsilon = whiskerLeft(Qh,eta.hom) followed by kappa into hshift. The shift equation for kappa rewrites its right side; cancel the shifted kappa component. Expand the composite-functor shift comparisons, use naturality of eta along the Qh shift isomorphism, and cancel its image under L. This is exactly the desired square at q(P). This argument uses the stipulated hshift directly, so it does not need a separate proof that shifted resolving complexes remain resolving.
Specialize the all-complex normalization equation to the single complex M[0]. No flatness of M is used.
